summary: concat returns a new array containing the receiver followed by the supplied arguments.
documentation: concat returns a new array containing the receiver followed by the supplied arguments. Array arguments contribute their elements one level deep; non-array arguments become single elements. It does not recursively flatten deeper nested arrays.
inputs: An object with first and second arrays of JSON values.
returns: A combined array, preserving nested items.
caution: The copy is shallow: referenced objects remain shared. Unlike push, concat does not mutate the input array.
scenarios: Combine two locally fetched result pages.
Append a separate group of checklist items to a working list.
Join ordered batches of invoice-line previews without editing either batch.
title: Combine two batches
problem: Input is {first, second}. Return first followed by second. Preserve duplicates, objects, null values and nested arrays exactly as elements; do not recursively flatten.
hint: Pass second as one array argument to first.concat.
goal: Use Array.concat() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
